All three shapes matter and each is a place a plausible implementation goes wrong: the shared native window helper this replaced (behavior_base.c level_window_allows, still used by C3DArrow, whose own consumer is not recovered) gave ExactLevel precedence over RequiredLevel, treated RequiredLevel -1 as blocked, and applied the window even to an ungated row. tools/linkage_oracles/CLoadLevel_gate.py compiles the real, unmodified behavior_load.c and drives it over all 97 shipped LOAD rows at 54 story states -- every RequiredLevel and ExactLevel value authored anywhere in the corpus with its two neighbours, plus 0, a value past the top of the story, and the store-absent case -- diffing all 5238 verdicts against the recovered rule evaluated on each row's own authored properties. Row identity is keyed on the file index over every object in the .gam, not over the LOAD rows alone, so a record-walk desync upstream of a portal surfaces as a mislabelled row instead of a silently shifted comparison.
